statements.justification: Accurate data, layers, and human macrophage citation [1] (PMID 32274896) that bridges two disconnected findings in Rubio 2021 (IL4 up-regulation and CD36/PPAR signaling) via a specific PPARgamma-dependent mechanism while noting flat serum IL-4.

All numbers, omic layers, cirrhosis design, and clinical citation [2] (PMID 31583743) are accurate; not 'Especially good' because serum IL-6 elevation and extra-blood-cell cytokine sources are already reported/discussed in Rubio 2021 and standard HE literature.

Data values, layers, design, and human macrophage citation [3] (PMID 27888289) are accurate and cautiously framed; connection between AHR and IL4 in the walk is only via a jump through CD36 and Ref [3] effector CCL1 is unmeasured in Table_S1.
Claim numbers, layers, and clinical MHE cohorts [4,5] (PMIDs 35032100, 26039496) are accurate; overlaps heavily with S2 and repeats serum IL-6 elevation already reported in Rubio 2021 Table 2.

Every value, direction, statistical relevance, and layer distinction for IL4 and TNF is exact, and the statement reflects cytokine transcript-protein discordance already noted generally in Rubio 2021 Discussion and Table_S3 (for TNF-a).

Two major errors: (D) IFNG is not significantly changed (+0.33, FDR=0.211) and leg 30 misread it as relevant +0.66, while Rubio 2021 explains PSME1 down-regulation via TNF (-0.45, FDR=0.020); (C) sole Ref [9] (PMID 18184038) studies HCV-infected hepatocytes/chimpanzee liver and demonstrates type I IFN—not IFN-γ—regulation of PA28.

Accurate expression values, blood-cell MHE-vs-noMHE framing, hematopoietic Meis1->FLT3 reference [10] (PMID 15755900), and cautious negative conclusion; minor internal step tag '(e39–e41)' and prose phrase 'at baseline' do not make the scientific claim wrong.

Tissue/species citation mismatch (C) and experimental-design conflation (X): uses a mouse CCl4 liver-fibrosis / HSC study [11] (PMID 37451016) to interpret peripheral blood-cell PDGFRB expression between already-cirrhotic MHE and noMHE patients, and leaks the baseline tag '(noMHE +0.76, relevant)' in an inverted way.

Biochemical error (B): misclassifies LIPA (lysosomal acid lipase / cholesteryl ester hydrolase, EC 3.1.1.13) as a post-squalene cholesterol-synthesis enzyme due to blindly reading KEGG hsa00100 edge DHCR7->LIPA, while omitting an actual altered synthesis enzyme (TM7SF2 -0.64, FDR=0.0093).

Citation tissue/cohort mismatch (C) and design conflation (X): applies hepatocyte VLDL-secretion [13] (PMID 35524581) and germline cirrhosis-predisposition [14] (PMID 41665936) studies to peripheral blood-cell APOB mRNA between patients who all already have cirrhosis (MHE vs noMHE), and leaks baseline label '(noMHE −0.97, relevant)'.

overall.comment: Five statements make sense (capturing serum IL-6 vs flat blood mRNA, IL4/TNF discordance, AHR/IL4, and HOXA9-MEIS1-FLT3), one is especially good (S1 links MHE IL4 and CD36 via PPARgamma-dependent macrophage signaling while catching flat serum IL-4), and four do not make sense: S6 claims non-significant IFNG (+0.33, FDR=0.21) is up and cites hepatocyte type-I IFN data, S9 misclassifies lysosomal hydrolase LIPA as a post-squalene cholesterol-synthesis enzyme, and S8/S10 import mouse hepatic stellate cell fibrosis and liver hepatocyte VLDL/cirrhosis studies into peripheral blood MHE-vs-noMHE comparisons.
